title: Session history: reload-pending is set before the reload is queued — so creation/destruction bookkeeping can reach the "navigationType is not null" assert

labels.name: compat
labels.description: Standard is not web compatible or proprietary feature needs standardizing

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

[Update for navigable creation/destruction](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#update-for-navigable-creation/destruction) applies the history step with a **null** _navigationType_, and step 11.1 of [apply the history step](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#apply-the-history-step) asserts that such a run never reaches the cross-document branch:

> 11. Otherwise:
>     1. Assert: _navigationType_ is not null.

But [reload](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#reload) sets the reload-pending flag **_before_** its own steps enter the session history traversal queue:

> 2. Set _navigable_’s active session history entry’s document state’s reload pending to true.
> 3. Let _traversable_ be _navigable_’s traversable navigable.
> 4. Append the following session history traversal steps to _traversable_: ...

So, any creation/destruction bookkeeping already sitting in the queue runs **between** those two steps, and picks up the pending reload:

1. The [changing-navigables selection](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#getting-the-used-step) appends the navigable — because its step 2 fires on reload-pending alone:
   > 2. If _targetEntry_ is not _navigable_’s current session history entry **or _targetEntry_’s document state’s reload pending is true**, then append _navigable_ to _results_.
2. The same flag then denies update-only:
   > 4. If _displayedEntry_ is _targetEntry_ **and _targetEntry_’s document state’s reload pending is false**, then: 1. Set _changingNavigableContinuation_’s update-only to true.
3. The navigable is therefore populated — producing a document that’s _not_ the displayed document. And so, step 10 (“update-only is true, or _targetEntry_’s document is _displayedDocument_”) does _not_ apply — and control reaches step 11, **where the assert fails.**

So nothing here is an implementation race. It just follows directly from the ordering the spec itself prescribes. A page that appends or removes an iframe in the same task that reloads another frame is enough to trigger it.

This caused LadybirdBrowser/ladybird#10893; it led to a crash in Ladybird on a real site — scrolling a page that churns ad iframes.

And in general it can be triggered by _any_ mechanism that leaves a navigable’s target entry calling for a cross-document change while a null-_navigationType_ run is queued reaches the same assert.

Another specific case this can hit is a consequence of [sync navigations jump queue](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#sync-navigations-jump-queue): A queue-jumping navigation supersedes an in-flight run’s step commit — after that run has already activated its target entries — leaving the current step selecting an entry other than a navigable’s active entry. So, the next bookkeeping run tries to populate that entry’s document. See the related issue at #12576.

### Implementations

https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/10900 is the fix made for this in Ladybird — to bring it in line with what other engines already do. No other engine performs a document change on a sibling frame because an unrelated frame was created or destroyed:

- **Blink** treats frame creation as history bookkeeping: adding a frame only prunes a stale `FrameNavigationEntry` from the last committed entry: [`frame_tree.cc`](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:content/browser/renderer_host/frame_tree.cc); scheduled reload is executed by the owning frame’s own task: [`http_refresh_scheduler.cc`](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:content/browser/renderer_host/http_refresh_scheduler.cc).
- **WebKit** routes document changes thru `recursiveGoToItem`; `recursiveSetProvisionalItem` only sets a provisional item where the frame already has the requested content: [`HistoryController.cpp`](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WebCore/loader/HistoryController.cpp), and reloads are driven from `NavigationScheduler`.
- **Gecko** applies frame add/remove to session-history structure only: [`nsSHistory.cpp`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/docshell/shistory/nsSHistory.cpp); reloads executed by a reloading docshell.

So, the assert in fact matches what engines actually do — but it’s the spec’s own step ordering that can violate it.


### Imaginable fixes

- Set the reload-pending flag **inside** the queued reload steps rather than before appending them, so no other queued run can observe it. That’d be the smallest change, and would match where the flag is consumed.
- Or have the changing-navigables selection ignore reload-pending when _navigationType_ is null — so a bookkeeping run never adopts another navigation’s work.
- Or define what a null-_navigationType_ run must do when a navigable’s target entry calls for a cross-document change: Skip it, or defer the bookkeeping until the owning run commits — rather than asserting it can’t happen.
- More broadly, if _“update for navigable creation/destruction”_ is meant to be pure bookkeeping, it may be worth saying so normatively, and scoping its changing-navigables selection to the created-or-destroyed navigable’s own subtree.
